```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["Original request, S1–S2"],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the service and test outcomes, boundaries, and defaults for discovery.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1 — Outcome [fact]: a small Python HTTP service lets organisers create events with a seat count and people reserve seats; successful reservations must respect available capacity. Boundary [fact]: the repository is empty, this unattended intake has no tools or files, and implementation is outside this stage. Delivery [assumption]: the usable target is the service in the source checkout; an isolated run’s checkout stays at its snapshot until final return, when the result becomes visible there. No deployed target is named; a deployed outcome would exist only after release. Open questions [recorded defaults, pending discovery]: (1) How are actors identified and access controlled? Discovery must first establish any runtime identity facilities; default to unauthenticated requests with no person identity, ruling out organiser-only permissions and per-person reservation limits. This choice blocks final authentication and authorization design until resolved. (2) How is state shared and how long does it live? Discovery must first establish the runtime and storage facilities; default to shared in-process state for the service lifetime, ending on process restart, ruling out persistence across restarts and sharing across service instances. This choice blocks final storage and deployment design until resolved. (3) What is hidden from whom? Discovery must first establish identity and data requirements; default to collecting no personal data and exposing only event and availability information through the service, ruling out private per-person reservation records. This choice blocks final response and privacy design until resolved. (4) What are the precise HTTP contracts and reservation rules? Discovery must first establish available runtime conventions and any existing requirements; default to a minimal event-creation and seat-reservation API that rejects invalid counts and prevents reservations beyond capacity, ruling out unrequested features. This choice blocks final endpoint and error contracts until resolved. Discovery source hints [unverified leads]: the eventual workspace and team, relevant channels, internal sites and documentation, private repositories, service owners, and the meanings of ‘organiser’, ‘reserve’, and ‘seat’; no specific source or owner is established by the request. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. S2 — Outcome [fact]: include tests covering the service’s requested behavior; they become usable in the returned source checkout alongside the service."
```
